text.title: llamaindex-chat-engine Core Rules
text.summary: Rules for selecting LlamaIndex chat-engine mode, bounding memory, and wiring streaming.

rule.statement: Default to chat_mode='condense_plus_context' for document-grounded multi-turn Q&A. It rewrites the follow-up question with conversation context before retrieval.
rule.rationale: condense_plus_context handles 'tell me more about that' follow-ups without needing tool use.

rule.statement: Use chat_mode='react' only when tool calls are required. ReAct adds 2-3 extra LLM calls per turn vs condense_plus_context.
rule.rationale: ReAct mode is expensive; reserve it for genuine multi-tool reasoning.

rule.statement: Bound conversation memory with ChatMemoryBuffer where token_limit is roughly half the context window. For an 8k context model, set token_limit=3900.
rule.rationale: Half the context window leaves room for retrieved chunks and the current question.

rule.statement: Instantiate a per-session ChatMemoryBuffer; never share a global instance across users.
rule.rationale: A shared buffer leaks history across users — same failure pattern as [[langchain-memory]] rule r13.

rule.statement: Enable streaming for chat UI; use chat_engine.stream_chat() not .chat().
rule.rationale: Perceived latency drops with first-token streaming; the difference for a chatbot is qualitative.

rule.statement: If a post-processor formats the answer after generation, choose either stream-and-no-postprocess OR no-stream-and-postprocess. Never both.
rule.rationale: Streaming + post-process produces UI flicker where the half-streamed answer jumps to the formatted final.

rule.statement: Pin the context_prompt template explicitly; never rely on LlamaIndex defaults for production. The defaults shift between minor releases.
rule.rationale: Default prompt changes have silently regressed user-facing answers across upgrades.

rule.statement: Verify session_id is a server-generated UUID, never client-supplied. Same rule as conversation memory across frameworks.
rule.rationale: Predictable session IDs let an attacker fetch another user's chat history.

rule.statement: When follow_up_complexity is high AND tool_use is required (the bot must call something beyond the index), the chat-engine-spec MUST set chat_mode='react' with an explicit tools list of QueryEngineTool / FunctionTool entries each carrying a name and description, pin max_iterations on the ReAct loop (check the current default for your version) so a confused agent cannot spin, attach a per-session ChatMemoryBuffer (r3, r4), and declare the expected LLM calls per turn (3 or more) against latency_target_ms. react MUST NOT be selected when the tools list is empty; that case is r-default-high.

rationale.source: LlamaIndex documentation (ReAct chat engine, ReActAgent, QueryEngineTool)

rule.rationale: ReAct reasons in a loop of thought / action / observation, so every turn costs 2-3 LLM calls more than condense_plus_context (r2, fm-02); paying that without tools buys nothing. Without a pinned iteration cap a tool that keeps returning unhelpful output turns one user turn into a dozen LLM calls and a latency budget miss.

rule.statement: When follow_up_complexity is high AND no tool use is required, the chat-engine-spec MUST set chat_mode='condense_plus_context' with both condense_prompt and context_prompt pinned to explicit templates (r7), similarity_top_k stated explicitly, a per-session ChatMemoryBuffer with token_limit at roughly half the context window (r3), and stream_chat() as the response path (r5). The measured LLM-call count per turn MUST be 2 (one condense, one answer) — the fm-02 detector. Neither 'context' mode (no question rewrite, so 'tell me more about that' retrieves on a pronoun) nor 'react' (r-advanced) is acceptable on this branch.

rationale.source: LlamaIndex documentation (Condense Plus Context chat engine)

rule.rationale: condense_plus_context rewrites the follow-up into a standalone question before retrieval, which is the only mode that makes anaphoric follow-ups retrieve the right chunks without an agent loop (r1). Leaving the two prompts at library defaults is how a minor upgrade silently changes the rewrite and regresses answers (r7).

rule.statement: When follow_up_complexity is low (follow-ups are self-contained or rare), the chat-engine-spec MUST set chat_mode='context': each user message is used verbatim as the retrieval query and the retrieved nodes go into a pinned system_prompt / context_prompt (r7), giving exactly 1 LLM call per turn. A per-session ChatMemoryBuffer with token_limit is still mandatory (r3, r4) so long sessions do not overflow the window. No condense step, no ReAct loop and no reranker are added on this branch; if the fm-02 detector counts more than 1 LLM call per turn the spec is wrong.
rule.rationale: For self-contained questions the condense call is pure cost: it doubles latency and token spend to rewrite a question that was already standalone. The memory bound still matters because 'low complexity' says nothing about session length, and an unbounded buffer is what produces fm-01's context-window blowup.
